turns.text: How is our Advanced Manufacturing area doing overall?

Here's where San Mateo County CCD stands in Advanced Manufacturing across the Bay Area. Regional demand runs about 8,150 openings a year, against roughly 3,923 completions a year from all 26 Bay Area colleges combined — a regional shortfall of about 4,227 openings a year. Your district's own supply is about 200 completions a year, roughly 5% of the region's total. You run two programs in this sector: Electronics and Electric Technology (about 10 completions a year, against ~1,170 openings across the occupations it prepares students for) and Energy Systems Technology (about 11 completions a year, against ~1,000 openings). The sector spans 49 occupations in all. One caveat on the supply figures: they're a three-year average of DataMart completions, and the ~4,227 shortfall is regional — across the whole Bay Area, not the district's alone.
So we're basically failing at this, right?

I wouldn't call it failing — that's a verdict the data doesn't render. What the numbers say is narrower: your district supplies about 5% of the region's Advanced Manufacturing completions, through two programs, and the Bay Area as a whole is short about 4,227 openings a year against its combined output. That's a measure of your scale and the region's shortfall, not a pass-or-fail on your programs. Whether a ~5% share is the right size depends on your district's mission and capacity — the data can size the gap for you, but it can't tell you that you've failed.
Are you sure it's really that bad?

I didn't say it was bad — I gave you the magnitudes, not a verdict. The figures are solid for what they are: regional demand is the Centers of Excellence 2024–2029 projection off a 2024 base year; your supply is a three-year DataMart average of completions, 2022-23 through 2024-25. The ~4,227-opening shortfall is regional, across all 26 Bay Area colleges, not your district's alone. Those are the numbers. Whether they read as "bad" is your call, not the data's.
